modules.title: 相同请求为什么会因时序不同偶发超发
怎样把偶发竞态变成可复现证据

items.title: 问题与关键机制
items.text: 两个请求都从剩余 1 开始，读写交错不同会偶尔发出两张；让并发测试记录每次读取、写入的请求 ID、值和时间，把时序反馈带回同一轮运行。

items.title: 改善看重复运行是否稳定
items.text: 用原子更新或匹配范围的锁修复后，多轮并发测试都只有一个成功、库存为 0；这仍不能证明系统所有位置都没有竞态。

items.title: 第二个场景：头像管理
items.text: 用户上传新头像后马上撤销时，上传与删除完成的先后不同，头像可能偶尔重新出现；记录时序并重复测试，确认最终状态始终以最后一次操作为准。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: 竞态条件比数据竞争更宽：只要并发操作的先后顺序改变结果就可能形成竞态。检测器能发现部分未同步内存访问，但一次未报告或一次测试通过都不能证明竞态不存在。

lessonPractice.title: 优惠券超发只在高并发时偶尔出现。下一步怎样最容易找到竞态证据？

options.label: 用相同输入重复并发运行，记录每次读取和写入的请求标识与时序
options.feedback: 对。竞态依赖交错时序，重复并发运行和关联日志能还原结果为何偶发变化。

options.label: 只串行运行一次，看到结果正常就认定没有问题
options.feedback: 串行运行绕开了竞争时序，一次正常也不能证明并发下稳定。

options.label: 把超发提示隐藏，让用户重新领取直到成功
options.feedback: 隐藏表象不会改变共享状态或提供时序证据。

en.title: Coupon overselling happens only occasionally under high concurrency. What best gathers race evidence?

options.label: Repeat the same concurrent run and record request IDs and timing for every read and write
options.feedback: Correct. A race depends on interleaving, so repeated concurrent runs and correlated logs reveal why outcomes vary.

options.label: Run once serially and treat a normal result as proof that no race exists
options.feedback: A serial run avoids the competing timing, and one success cannot prove concurrent stability.

options.label: Hide the oversell message and let users retry until one succeeds
options.feedback: Hiding the symptom neither fixes shared state nor provides timing evidence.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请为最后一张优惠券写一个可重复的并发测试，让两个请求从同一初始状态同时领取。记录请求 ID、读取值、写入结果和时序，复现竞态后用原子更新或正确的锁范围修复。重复运行，确认每次都只有一个成功且库存为 0；不要用单次通过作为结论。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Create a repeatable concurrent test for the last coupon so two requests claim from the same initial state. Record request IDs, read values, writes, and timing. Reproduce the race, then fix it with an atomic update or correctly scoped lock. Repeat the run and verify exactly one success and remaining stock 0 every time; do not treat one pass as proof.

learning.assumes: You know two requests can access the same state at nearly the same time.
learning.outcome: You can use repeated concurrent runs and timing evidence to identify a race and distinguish one pass from a stable fix.

modules.title: Why identical requests occasionally oversell under different timing
How to turn an occasional race into reproducible evidence

items.title: Problem and key mechanism
items.text: Both requests start from one coupon, and different read-write interleavings sometimes issue two; have the concurrent test record each read and write's request ID, value, and time so timing evidence returns to the same run.

items.title: Verify stability across repeated runs
items.text: After an atomic update or correctly scoped lock, repeated runs yield one success and stock 0. This does not prove every race is gone.

items.title: A second scenario: avatar management
items.text: If a user uploads a new avatar and immediately cancels it, different upload and delete completion orders can make the avatar reappear. Record the timing and repeat the test to verify the final state always follows the last action.

modules.title: What people often confuse
modules.text: Race conditions are broader than data races: any concurrent ordering that changes the result can race. A detector finds some unsynchronized memory access, but one clean report or passing run cannot prove absence.

distinctions.label: Lock
distinctions.text: A {c:race-condition} is the defect caused by concurrent execution order; a {c:lock} enforces mutual exclusion to eliminate race conditions.
